pages.text:
Coherent Launches PhotonLink™ Integrated Optics Platform for AI Infrastructure
SAXONBURG, Pa., Sept. 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Coherent Corp. (NYSE: COHR), the global leader in photonics, today announced PhotonLink™, an integrated optics platform that brings together Coherent’s broad portfolio of critical photonics technologies, precision assembly and test capabilities to deliver complete optical solutions for next-generation AI datacenters. The platform supports co-packaged optics (CPO), near-packaged optics (NPO) and emerging chip to chip connectivity.
As AI systems continue to scale, demand for higher bandwidth and lower power is driving optical connectivity closer to compute and switching silicon. These architectures require lasers, silicon photonics, precision optics, fibers and detectors to work together. PhotonLink brings those technologies and the expertise to integrate them into one platform.
“The next leap in AI requires more than faster chips – it requires a new way to connect them,” said Jim Anderson, Chief Executive Officer at Coherent. “Customers need complete optical solutions, not just individual components. Coherent is uniquely positioned to bring together the critical technologies, integrate and test the finished assemblies, and manufacture them at scale. PhotonLink puts that capability to work for the next generation of AI infrastructure.”
Coherent’s vertical integration spans compound semiconductor materials, lasers, optics and specialty fiber through final assembly and test. PhotonLink gives customers access to both individual components and complete optical assemblies from one partner, helping simplify system design, streamline qualification and reduce the complexity of integrating technologies from multiple suppliers.
FROM CRITICAL TECHNOLOGIES TO COMPLETE OPTICAL ASSEMBLIES
The PhotonLink platform spans four functions of the optical path: Generate, Shape, Guide and Receive. The portfolio includes indium phosphide (InP) lasers, vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL) arrays, silicon photonics, isolators, specialty fibers, micro-optics and detectors. Coherent integrates these technologies into external laser sources, precision fiber assemblies and optical modules tailored to customer architectures.
CUSTOMER ENGAGEMENT AND MANUFACTURING SCALE
Coherent has more than ten CPO customer engagements and more than ten NPO engagements, with anchor customers and long-term agreements secured for both architectures. The company also has more than five engagements in emerging chip to chip connectivity. Revenue from the PhotonLink platform is expected to begin ramping in Q4 of CY2026.
PhotonLink builds on Coherent’s established datacenter manufacturing base, which has shipped more than 300 million InP lasers and more than one billion InP and gallium arsenide (GaAs) photodetectors. Coherent is expanding its 6” InP and specialty fiber manufacturing capacity to support the PhotonLink ramp.
Coherent hosted a PhotonLink launch event on September 21 at the Gran Hotel Miramar in Málaga during the European Conference on Optical Communication (ECOC) 2026. The presentation and webcast recording are available at PHOTONLINK™ Launch webcast
Visitors to ECOC 2026 can also meet Coherent experts and explore PhotonLink at Stand 2100, Hall 2, at FYCMA - Trade Fair & Congress Center in Málaga, Spain.
For more information about PhotonLink, visit https://www.coherent.com/datacenter-communications/photonlink
Coherent is the global photonics leader. We harness photons to drive innovation. Industry leaders in the datacenter, communications, and industrial markets rely on Coherent’s world-leading technology to fuel their own innovation and growth. Founded in 1971 and operating in more than 20 countries, Coherent brings the industry’s broadest, deepest technology stack; unmatched supply chain resilience; and global scale to help its customers solve their toughest technology challenges. For more information, visit coherent.com.

Is Coherent (COHR) Fairly Valued?
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 9:15 PM CDT 4 min read
Coherent (NYSE:COHR) reports its fiscal first-quarter results early next month, and it has already set a high bar. Management told investors to expect revenue between $2.2 billion and $2.4 billion, up from the $2.05 billion it reported last quarter.
But the stock is priced as if that growth might not last. It trades at about 24.7 times estimated fiscal 2027 earnings, which is below its own five-year average. Consensus still calls for strong adjusted earnings growth that year. A faster-growing business at a lower multiple than its history raises the question of whether investors are being too cautious.
Coherent makes the lasers, optical parts, and networking components that move data inside AI data centers and across telecom networks. Its Datacenter & Communications segment, by far its largest, brought in $1.615 billion last quarter, up from $1.018 billion a year earlier. The results lean toward a stock that is cheaper than they justify, with one big condition: its customers have to keep spending.
Data Center Sales Are Driving the Growth
Growth has sped up sharply. Over the past five years, Coherent's revenue grew about 18% a year, and last quarter it rose 34% from a year earlier, well above that pace. On a pro forma basis, which adjusts for businesses Coherent has sold, the quarter's growth was 42%.
The product mix is moving the same way. Last month, Coherent launched PhotonLink, a platform that bundles its lasers, detectors, and other optical parts for AI data centers. Yahoo Finance reported that the company counts 20 customer engagements so far, and that Nvidia invested about $4 billion in Coherent and Lumentum earlier this year. For investors looking to add exposure to AI data center optics, our list of 10 Best Fiber Optics Stocks to Buy for the AI Data Center Boom is worth a look.
Nvidia Backed a $50 Billion AI Data-Center IPO. Wall Street Just Hit the Brakes
Adjusted operating margin reached 21.8% last quarter, up from 18.0% a year earlier, so each dollar of new sales kept more profit. Adjusted earnings per share rose $0.74 from a year earlier, to $1.74. Investors who want more high-growth stocks can see our ranking of 10 Best Aggressive Growth Stocks to Buy According to Wall Street Analysts.
The adjusted figure runs well above the GAAP one: GAAP earnings per share were $1.19 last quarter, against $1.74 on the adjusted basis. Earnings estimates, and the multiple built on them, use the adjusted number, so the gap matters to anyone paying for the stock.
Most of the growth comes from AI data centers, so a pause in spending by the companies building them would reach Coherent quickly. Management described customer demand in its latest release as exceptional, and its guidance for the coming quarter sits above what it just reported. One reading of the lower multiple is that buyers want a discount for that dependence. The next report will show whether demand is still arriving at that level.
What Investors Are Paying for That Growth
At about 24.7 times estimated earnings for the fiscal year ending next June, Coherent trades above the 21.01 median for its sector. It sits below its own five-year average of 27.46. Against expected adjusted earnings growth of about 68% for the same year, the premium to its sector looks small. If you're looking for cheaper AI names, check out 10 Undervalued AI Stocks to Buy Now.
The price assumes that growth will slow or that customer spending will stall before those earnings arrive. If you own the stock, you own it at a lower price against earnings than it has usually carried, in exchange for taking on that spending risk.
Are investors being too cautious? Faster sales, wider margins, and a multiple below the stock's own history suggest they are pricing in more doubt than the numbers show. Next month's report is the thing to watch: whether revenue lands in the guided range, and whether the data center business keeps growing at last quarter's pace.
While we acknowledge the risk and potential of COHR as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. If you are looking for an AI stock that is more promising than COHR and that has 10,000% upside potential, check out our report about this cheapest AI stock.

Optics Names Advance on Earnings Anticipation
Applied Optoelectronics shares led the session’s gains among the three. Lumentum stock also posted a solid advance. Coherent Benefits From AI Networking Focus
Coherent stock rose more modestly. The company has launched its PhotonLink integrated optics platform designed for co-packaged optics, near-packaged optics, and chip-to-chip connectivity. Coherent already has more than 10 customer engagements in these areas, with initial PhotonLink revenue expected to ramp in the December quarter.
Coherent can benefit from existing high-speed optical transceiver demand even if broader co-packaged optics adoption takes longer than expected. The Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF’s gain reflected measured interest across the specialty group. Photonic integrated circuits are seeing rapid expansion tied to high-speed data transmission and energy-efficient optical technologies for AI data centers. Market forecasts point to strong compound annual growth rates through the end of the decade as cloud and hyperscale operators scale optical infrastructure.
Similarities among Applied Optoelectronics, Lumentum, and Coherent include exposure to AI networking demand and optical components for data centers. Differences appear in product focus and scale, with Lumentum highlighting multiyear sold-out conditions, Coherent emphasizing integrated platforms, and Applied Optoelectronics concentrating on specific optical modules. The broader chip sector has also shown signs of stabilizing after a recent soft stretch.
Upcoming earnings will provide the next major checkpoints for order visibility and margin trends across the three companies. Lumentum’s multiyear capacity constraints and Coherent’s PhotonLink ramp offer potential catalysts if demand remains robust. Applied Optoelectronics faces similar questions around AI optical adoption and competitive positioning.
Investors should consider keeping their position sizes modest given the volatility typical of optics and photonics stocks. Stronger-than-expected guidance or further evidence of sold-out conditions could support the shares, while any signs of softer demand or elevated valuations may pressure the group after the recent run.

Global optical fiber demand is projected to reach 577 million fiber-kilometers in 2026, with data centers accounting for a growing share.

TrendForce forecasts a global optical fiber supply shortfall of 180 million fiber-kilometers in 2026.
Spot prices for bend-insensitive fiber used inside data centers are projected to average more than five times their 2025 levels.
Expanding optical fiber preform capacity typically takes 18 to 24 months, limiting how quickly manufacturers can respond.

Shares of Corning Inc. (GLW) and Verizon Communications Inc. (VZ) are in focus after research firm TrendForce forecast on Monday that rising artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure demand would leave the global optical fiber market facing a supply shortfall of 180 million fiber-kilometers in 2026.
The firm expects shortages to persist until at least 2028. Separately, it projects spot prices for finished optical fiber products to reach 2.8 to more than five times their 2025 levels in 2026, depending on the fiber type.
ASTS Stock Jumps Overnight: CFO Gets New 3-Year Contract — Here’s What’s In His Pay And Exit Package
Other fiber-related stocks also came into focus, including Coherent (COHR), Ciena (CIEN), and Amphenol (APH), given their exposure to fiber-optic connectivity, optical components and high-capacity networking infrastructure.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
According to TrendForce, global optical fiber demand is expected to reach 577 million fiber-kilometers this year, with data centers accounting for roughly 18% to 20% of consumption. That share is projected to climb to 30% to 35% in 2027.
TrendForce said AI data-center demand has tightened global supply since late 2025, with chipmakers and telecom operators joining hyperscale cloud providers in investing in related infrastructure.
Unlike previous telecom infrastructure cycles, the firm said the current shortage reflects sustained additional demand from AI data centers, driving the need for interconnects and high-capacity backbone networks.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Global optical fiber capacity utilization has climbed to 92%, while inventories have fallen from four months in 2024 to just one month. Some leading suppliers are already booked into the first quarter of 2027, while expanding preform capacity typically takes 18 to 24 months.
The pricing impact varies by application. Bend-insensitive fiber used inside data centers is projected to average more than five times its 2025 price, while AI backbone fiber prices are expected to reach approximately 2.8 times their 2025 levels. Mainstream telecom fiber quotations could rise to around 3.7 times their previous levels.
Corning, Verizon Lock In Long-Term Fiber Supply
TrendForce said telecom operators are already shifting from short-term purchases to long-term supply agreements to secure future fiber requirements.

The firm highlighted a September agreement between Corning and Verizon covering approximately 129 million fiber kilometers, or 80 million fiber miles, of high-density optical fiber and connectivity solutions.
Corning also signed a separate agreement worth more than $3 billion with AT&T (T) in September to supply fiber and cable for its U.S. network expansion.
TrendForce expects such agreements to become increasingly common as AI-related demand continues to grow and manufacturers face lengthy capacity expansion timelines.

Coherent Has Massively Diappointed Investors for 6 Months: A Respected Analyst Predicts It Will Double Moving Forward
Coherent keeps beating earnings estimates while its stock slides further from a 52-week high, and now Wall Street's most bullish analyst has a target that implies shares could nearly double from here.
Published October 15, 2026, 8:45am ET · 4 min read
A dynamic stock market screen with an upward trend signifies the optimistic outlook for companies like Applied Optoelectronics, as analysts predict significant gains. © Travis Wolfe / Shutterstock.com
Coherent (NYSE:COHR | COHR Price Prediction) is priced at $263.23, while the average analyst price target sits at $412.52. The difference points to about 56.7% upside.
Coherent makes lasers, optical transceivers and photonic components. Its Datacenter & Communications division now brings in 79% of revenue. With funding from NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA), which invested $2B, Coherent also joined the S&P 500 during fiscal 2026.
The gap matters because the business keeps speeding up while the stock goes the other way. With implied upside above 40%, Wall Street is saying the market has mispriced one of the main suppliers of AI connectivity.
Record Quarters and Falling Shares Open a Six-Month Disconnect
Most of the decline came in a single week. Coherent fell 21.32% over the past week, including a 9.22% drop in the latest session. That session came right after a hot inflation report drove the 30-year Treasury yield as high as 5.63%. AI infrastructure names fell, a cloud provider falling 16% and a server maker 11%. Rising rates hit capital-hungry suppliers hardest. Coherent spent $1.103B on capex in fiscal 2026 but generated only $79.5M in operating cash flow.
Over six months, shares are down 15.98%, and the stock trades about 40% below its 52-week high of $440. Optics stocks fell on profit taking with no company news behind it. Earlier, a fiber maker’s $2B at-the-market equity offering dragged Coherent 11% lower in sympathy.
Coherent’s own results stayed strong. Coherent has beaten EPS estimates 4 consecutive times. Its latest quarter delivered non-GAAP EPS of $1.74 versus $1.6171 expected, on revenue up 33.7%.
Rosenblatt’s $500 Target Calls for Shares to Nearly Double
Mike Genovese at Rosenblatt Securities holds the highest target on Wall Street at $500.00 with a Buy rating. That target means 89.9% upside. His thesis rests on three things: an AI transceiver super-cycle, production that is sold out well in advance, and margins that expand as manufacturing scale catches up with demand.
Management’s own comments support that view. “Fiscal 27 is basically completely booked out,” the CEO said. Customer orders reach into calendar 28, and long-term agreements run through the end of the decade. Coherent expects its first quarter above $3 billion in revenue by the end of fiscal 2027. Current-quarter guidance calls for revenue of $2.20B to $2.40B and EPS of $1.85 to $2.05.
Analysts are watching specific catalysts. Indium phosphide output is set to double this quarter, one quarter ahead of plan. Co-packaged optics revenue begins ramping in fiscal Q2. Optical circuit switching targets more than $4 billion of addressable market. Management also keeps its gross margin target above 42%.
Of 24 analysts, 4 have it at Strong Buy, 15 at Buy and 5 at Hold, with zero Sells. Bernstein recently started coverage at Outperform (247 Wall St.). Still, targets are estimates and carry no guarantee. The trailing P/E of 68x against a forward P/E of 30x shows how much of the thesis depends on earnings that have yet to arrive.
Fabrinet Carries the Optics Group’s Deepest Discount
The whole peer group sold off together. Coherent’s decline is a sector event.
Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE) fell 19.33% over the past week but remains up 143.18% year to date. At $896.33 against a $1177.34 target, implied upside is 31.4%, which is smaller than Coherent’s. Coverage is heavily bullish, with 5 Strong Buys, 18 Buys and 4 Holds.
Fabrinet (NYSE:FN) dropped 21.09% for the week and is down 13.69% year to date. At $392.93 against a $734.11 target, it shows 86.8% implied upside. Coverage is lighter, with 3 Strong Buys, 4 Buys and 2 Holds among 9 analysts.
Fabrinet carries the largest consensus upside in the group. Coherent sits in the middle, offering a bigger discount than Lumentum with wider coverage than Fabrinet.
Coherent Still Beats the S&P 500 Despite the Slide
At $263.23, Coherent trades well below the $412.52 consensus target, leaving 56.7% implied upside across 24 covering analysts.
The six-month decline of 15.98% hides a strong year. Shares are up 42.62% year to date, while the S&P 500 has gained 12.86%. Over one year, Coherent is up 140.68%.
Coherent’s Booked Backlog Outweighs the Rate Risk
The bullish case improves if Coherent keeps converting its sold-out backlog into revenue on schedule and gross margin keeps climbing toward 42%. The outlook weakens if long-term rates keep rising, the heavy capex keeps burning cash, or hyperscaler spending cools off before co-packaged optics and optical circuit switching reach scale.
A $3 billion quarter and margin expansion would make the consensus target look conservative. On the risk side, Coherent carries about $3.2B of long-term debt and a beta of 2.113, so every move in rates gets amplified.
Contracted demand into calendar 2028 suggests this selloff reflects a rate and sentiment reset. The stock’s high beta points to continued volatility.

Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) chief executive Lip-Bu Tan also pointed to rising borrowing costs and uncertainty over returns on AI investments. Along with other optical names, Lumentum stock finished among the market’s biggest losers that day.
The selling has continued since, and no company-specific development explains this session’s move in Applied Optoelectronics stock. Applied Optoelectronics completed an at-the-market equity program, raising capital to fund the capacity expansion its optical component business needs. Its completion announcement came on October 5, days before the funding warnings from Broadcom and Intel.
Smallest Supplier Faces the Biggest Capacity Test
Lasers, transceivers and optical components from Applied Optoelectronics, Coherent and Lumentum move data between servers inside AI data centers. Their revenue tracks hyperscale spending. So the group is sensitive to any sign that budgets could tighten (we covered seven non-chipmaker suppliers riding the same AI expansion in a free report here). By far the smallest of the group, Applied Optoelectronics also sells into cable broadband networks, which gives it a revenue base Coherent and Lumentum don’t share.
Record results support the bull case. In Q2 2026, Applied Optoelectronics posted revenue of $191.92 million, up 86.4% year over year, as its datacenter segment more than doubled. The company also returned to adjusted profitability, earning $0.06 per share against a $0.015 estimate.
On the company’s August 6 call, chief executive Thompson Lin stated, “Demand to support next-generation AI infrastructure remains so robust that our near-term revenue is bounded almost entirely by production capacity and key component availability.” Management then guided Q3 2026 revenue to $255 million to $290 million. Lin also forecast that demand would outpace production capacity through mid-2027.
Hyperscale Orders Decide the Expansion Payoff
The open question for Applied Optoelectronics is whether hyperscale customers keep placing orders at the pace its expanded capacity assumes. Its top 10 customers accounted for 99% of Q2 2026 revenue, which leaves little buffer if one large buyer slows down its spending or delays deliveries. Applied Optoelectronics still posted a net loss under generally accepted accounting principles in that quarter, a reminder that its rapid expansion is costly.
Coherent and Lumentum struck a confident tone in August. On an August 12 call, Coherent chief executive Jim Anderson stated, “We continue to see no signs of attenuation in customer demand.” Lumentum chief executive Michael Hurlston added that “data center architects are turning to optical links as a primary means of connectivity,” and the company guided Q1 FY2027 revenue to $1.225 billion to $1.275 billion.
Those remarks came weeks before the funding warnings from Broadcom and Intel, so fresh order commentary from these suppliers could show whether this pullback reflects a real shift in demand. For now, investors may want to keep their exposure to optical names appropriately sized for further volatility.

Coherent Jumps 10% on PhotonLink Push and Bernstein’s Outperform Start; Lumentum Rises 9%, Corning Advances 3%
Coherent's PhotonLink platform and a fresh Wall Street initiation sent optics stocks surging well ahead of the broader market, raising the question of whether this rally signals a durable AI infrastructure trade or another sentiment-driven spike.
Published October 1, 2026, 10:56am ET · 3 min read
Coherent Corp. (NYSE:COHR | COHR Price Prediction) stock jumped 10% to $315.71 as traders focused on the company’s PhotonLink platform and fresh Wall Street support for AI infrastructure suppliers. Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) stock rose 9% to $1,058.42, while Corning (NYSE:GLW) stock advanced 3% to $158.89.
The broader optics rally outpaced the market. The Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF (CBOE:LYTE) gained 4% to $25.40, while the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE ARCA:SPY) slipped 0.2% to $761.11.
Coherent introduced PhotonLink in September as an integrated-optics platform for next-generation AI data centers. The company also expanded its Pluggable Optical Line System portfolio, linking chip-to-chip, inside-the-rack, and high-capacity data-center connectivity products to the same AI infrastructure buildout.
PhotonLink highlights Coherent’s vertically integrated position across materials, lasers, optics, specialty fibers, and related manufacturing capabilities. Coherent said the platform includes more than 10 customer engagements for co-packaged optics and more than 10 customer engagements for near-packaged optics.
AI data centers require more bandwidth and more efficient connections as workloads become larger and more complex. Coherent could benefit if hyperscalers and equipment makers accelerate deployments of advanced optical components, though the company must turn early engagement into sustained orders and profitable production.
Bernstein initiated coverage of Coherent with an Outperform rating as part of broader coverage of U.S. networking and optical companies. Bernstein said networking and optical suppliers could be “structural winners” within AI infrastructure, an assessment that helped reinforce investor interest in Coherent stock.
The research firm also began coverage of Lumentum, Ciena Corporation (NYSE:CIEN), and Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET) with Outperform ratings. Bernstein initiated Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) and Corning with Market Perform ratings, providing a more balanced view of an industry that has rallied sharply on AI-related expectations.
Coherent stock’s 10% gain exceeded the 4% move in the LYTE ETF, suggesting that PhotonLink and Bernstein’s favorable initiation gave traders a company-specific reason to bid up the shares. Still, Coherent stock can remain sensitive to shifts in AI capital-spending expectations, customer order timing, and concerns about industry capacity.
Lumentum stock climbed 9% to $1,058.42, extending the recovery that began after a recent optics-sector selloff. Lumentum reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $1.006 billion, up 109.3% year over year, while adjusted earnings per share of $3.23 exceeded the $2.97 consensus estimate.
The company guided for fiscal first-quarter revenue between $1.225 billion and $1.275 billion. Lumentum management said demand signals for 2027 remained “incredibly strong,” while the company also reported that optical-circuit-switch shipments doubled from the fiscal third quarter to the fiscal fourth quarter.
Lumentum could benefit from demand for high-speed networking, optical switching, transceivers, and other hardware needed to connect AI computing systems. Yet Lumentum faces execution risk as the company expands output, with management previously acknowledging that shipments of high-powered lasers were behind demand.
Corning stock rose 3%, a smaller gain than Coherent stock and Lumentum stock but still well ahead of the SPY ETF’s 0.2% decline. Corning supplies specialty glass, fiber, and optical communications products, giving Corning multiple ways to participate in higher data-center connectivity spending.
The LYTE ETF’s 4% advance suggests the market’s buying interest extended beyond a single company. Coherent stock, Lumentum stock, and Corning stock all moved higher as traders returned to a group that benefits from expectations for rising AI network traffic and increasingly demanding data-center architectures.
The Coherent stock rally could continue if AI-related orders, customer commentary, and capital-spending plans remain supportive. However, the same theme creates risk if large customers delay infrastructure spending, if competitors build excess capacity, or if elevated expectations leave less room for execution mistakes.
Coherent has a compelling product catalyst in PhotonLink and a new Outperform rating to support the bullish discussion. Investors should watch for signs that the company’s customer engagements become material revenue opportunities, while keeping position sizes modest because optics stocks can move sharply as sentiment toward the AI trade changes.

CRDO vs. COHR: Which AI Connectivity Stock Is the Better Buy?
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:14 AM CDT 7 min read
Both Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd CRDO and Coherent Corp COHR are beneficiaries of the AI data center buildout, but approach the opportunity from different angles.
Credo specializes in high-speed connectivity solutions, including integrated circuits (ICs), retimers, optical DSPs, Active Electrical Cables (AECs), SerDes chiplets and SerDes IP licensing.
Coherent is a manufacturer of lasers, transceivers, optoelectronic devices and modules, and engineered materials for verticals spanning industrial, instrumentation, communications and electronics markets.
For investors, the choice between CRDO and COHR is not straightforward. Let us break down the fundamentals, valuations, growth outlook and risks for each company to determine which stock stands out.
As AI clusters grow larger, connectivity is emerging as a critical constraint. Management highlighted that the challenge is no longer just bandwidth, but also reliability, power efficiency, signal integrity, telemetry and serviceability. Credo believes its system-level approach, which combines silicon, firmware, manufacturing tests and qualification, remains a key differentiator.
AEC is a system-level product for CRDO and its core growth engine. The company now has deep relationships with five hyperscalers, alongside expanding engagement with Neocloud customers. Credo continues to see higher AEC penetration within existing customers as deployments scale, while the shift toward 200-gig-per-lane 1.6T ports provides another growth opportunity.
The retimer business is another lucrative opportunity. Management noted that the retimer business also delivered record quarterly revenues, supported by scale-up deployments of Screaming Eagle at 100-gig-per-lane and initial contributions from its 200-gig-per-lane Blue Heron retimer.
The most significant shift in Credo's business mix is unfolding in its optical segment. On the last earnings call, management added that it continues to project more than $600 million in optical revenues, with ZeroFlap optics, silicon photonics PICs and optical DSPs each contributing over $100 million. Credo added that its optical DSP business generated "record revenues" in the fiscal first quarter. The company also recognized its first silicon-photonics PIC revenues following the DustPhotonics acquisition, with initial wins involving 800-gig and 1.6T optical transceivers. Credo continues to forecast more than 85% year-over-year revenue growth for fiscal 2027, aided by an expected second-half inflection.
The company's recent product announcements further strengthen its growth prospects. At the October 2026 OCP Global Summit, the company introduced its 1.6T ZeroFlap Active Light Cable ("ALC"). The wide-parallel optical interconnect solution is built for next-generation AI infrastructure, addressing rising reliability and energy-efficiency requirements. The solution targets AI scale-out and front-end networks, strengthening Credo's position in next-generation optical interconnects. Shipments are expected to begin in 2027.
Alongside the new ALC, the company announced the launch of the Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics Workstream within the Open Compute Project community. The initiative, backed by a leading hyperscaler and optical technology providers, including AFL, ams OSRAM and BizLink, aims to advance the development of the wide, parallel optical connectivity ecosystem.
The latest developments build on the company's expanding product portfolio. In September 2026, Credo launched its new family of 224G-based ZF optical transceivers. The new products extend Credo's ZF architecture to 1.6T port speeds and combine its 224G-per-lane optical DSP with the Kfir200 silicon photonics-based PICs and latest-generation PILOT diagnostics platform. The products are available in 2xDR4, 2xFR4 and DR8 configurations, supporting a range of AI scale-out interconnect architectures.
CRDO's growth does not come without meaningful risks. In the fiscal first quarter, four customers generated roughly 84% of quarterly revenues. Customer concentration is a major concern as it exposes the company to shifts in customer spending decisions and could materially affect results.
Execution risk is another risk factor. Much of the expected growth in fiscal 2027 is dependent on a successful ramp in the optical business. Any delay in deployment or broader industry transitions could affect this ramp. Macroeconomic uncertainties and exposure to the AI investment cycle amid increasing market competition remain additional concerns. The DustPhotonics acquisition also reduced its cash balance to $764.3 million at the end of the fiscal first quarter.
Explosive growth in AI data center infrastructure is driving unprecedented demand for optical networking solutions, positioning Coherent for long-term growth.
The Datacenter & Communications segment remains Coherent's core engine, contributing 79% of total revenues in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. Segment revenues increased 59% year over year, while data center revenues surged 66% on broad-based strength. Growing adoption of 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers bodes well. Management expects the 1.6T transceiver ramp to accelerate in calendar 2026 and 2027 as customer adoption increases.
Coherent expects first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues between $2.2 billion and $2.4 billion, with non-GAAP earnings per share of $1.85-$2.05. The company expects to achieve its first-ever quarter with over $3 billion in revenue by the end of fiscal 2027.
The launch of PhotonLink strengthens its product portfolio. This integrated optics platform combines lasers, silicon photonics, specialty fibers, isolators, specialty fibers, micro-optics and detectors to support co-packaged optics ("CPO"), near-packaged optics ("NPO") and emerging chip-to-chip connectivity. PhotonLink-related revenues are expected to begin ramping in the fourth quarter of calendar 2026.
Beyond transceivers, CPO, multi-rail systems, optical circuit switching ("OCS") and advanced materials for data center, thermal and power management offer additional growth opportunities. OCS revenues increased sequentially in the fiscal fourth quarter, while multi-rail revenues are expected to begin ramping in the first half of calendar 2027. The company expects OCS revenues to improve, supported by capacity expansion, in the upcoming quarters.
On the last earnings call, COHR noted that OCS represented more than $4 billion of addressable opportunity across data center interconnect, scale-up and scale-out networks. Further, management added that CPO, NPO and other forms of integrated optics represent more than $15 billion of incremental addressable opportunity over the coming years as these technologies enable the transition from copper connectivity.
Aggressive capacity expansion strategy bodes well. On the last earnings call, management said that the company was expanding its six-inch indium phosphide production capacity, targeting a doubling of internal output year over year by the end of the first quarter of fiscal 2027. Management expects capacity to more than double again by the end of calendar 2027.
However, the company is witnessing rising operating and capital expenses as it focuses on capacity expansion. While these investments are necessary for long-term growth, they may pressure margins and free cash flow if revenues do not materialize as expected. Capital expenditures reached $556 million in the fiscal fourth quarter, compared with $290 million in the preceding quarter, and management expects further sequential increase in the fiscal first quarter.
Heavy reliance on the Datacenter & Communications segment increases volatility linked to AI spending cycles amid increasing competition and macroeconomic troubles. Weakness in the Industrial segment, owing to softness in broader industrial markets, is concerning.
Price Performance & Valuations of CRDO & COHR
Year to date, CRDO and COHR are up 24.5% and 42.6%, respectively.
CRDO is trading at a forward price-to-earnings multiple of 23.41X, lower than COHR's 24.73X.
How Do the Consensus Estimates Compare for CRDO & COHR?
Analysts have raised their earnings estimates for COHR by 0.9% for the current fiscal year in the past 60 days.
Estimates have been revised up 4.2% for CRDO's bottom line in the same period.
CRDO offers strong revenue growth prospects but customer concentration and execution risks remain concerns. COHR benefits from a broader optical portfolio, expanding manufacturing capacity and strong AI-driven demand, though rising capital expenditures could pressure cash flow.
COHR carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) while CRDO carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). Coherent appears to be a better pick now based on the Zacks Rank.

Most of the decline came in a single week. Coherent fell 21.32% over the past week, including a 9.22% drop in the latest session. Mike Genovese at Rosenblatt Securities holds the highest target on Wall Street at $500.00 with a Buy rating. That target means 89.9% upside. Management's own comments support that view. "Fiscal 27 is basically completely booked out," the CEO said. Customer orders reach into calendar 28, and long-term agreements run through the end of the decade. Coherent expects its first quarter above $3 billion in revenue by the end of fiscal 2027. Current-quarter guidance calls for revenue of $2.20B to $2.40B and EPS of $1.85 to $2.05.
Analysts are watching specific catalysts. Indium phosphide output is set to double this quarter, one quarter ahead of plan. Co-packaged optics revenue begins ramping in fiscal Q2. Optical circuit switching targets more than $4 billion of addressable market. Management also keeps its gross margin target above 42%.
Of 24 analysts, 4 have it at Strong Buy, 15 at Buy and 5 at Hold, with zero Sells. Bernstein recently started coverage at Outperform (247 Wall St.). Still, targets are estimates and carry no guarantee. The trailing P/E of 68x against a forward P/E of 30x shows how much of the thesis depends on earnings that have yet to arrive.
Fabrinet Carries the Optics Group's Deepest Discount
The whole peer group sold off together. Coherent's decline is a sector event.
Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE) fell 19.33% over the past week but remains up 143.18% year to date. At $896.33 against a $1177.34 target, implied upside is 31.4%, which is smaller than Coherent's. Coverage is heavily bullish, with 5 Strong Buys, 18 Buys and 4 Holds.

Fabrinet carries the largest consensus upside in the group. Coherent sits in the middle, offering a bigger discount than Lumentum with wider coverage than Fabrinet.
Coherent Still Beats the S&P 500 Despite the Slide
At $263.23, Coherent trades well below the $412.52 consensus target, leaving 56.7% implied upside across 24 covering analysts.
The six-month decline of 15.98% hides a strong year. Shares are up 42.62% year to date, while the S&P 500 has gained 12.86%. Over one year, Coherent is up 140.68%.
Coherent's Booked Backlog Outweighs the Rate Risk
The bullish case improves if Coherent keeps converting its sold-out backlog into revenue on schedule and gross margin keeps climbing toward 42%. The outlook weakens if long-term rates keep rising, the heavy capex keeps burning cash, or hyperscaler spending cools off before co-packaged optics and optical circuit switching reach scale.
A $3 billion quarter and margin expansion would make the consensus target look conservative. On the risk side, Coherent carries about $3.2B of long-term debt and a beta of 2.113, so every move in rates gets amplified.
Contracted demand into calendar 2028 suggests this selloff reflects a rate and sentiment reset. The stock's high beta points to continued volatility.

The gap matters because the business keeps speeding up while the stock goes the other way. With implied upside above 40%, Wall Street is saying the market has mispriced one of the main suppliers of AI connectivity.
Record Quarters and Falling Shares Open a Six-Month Disconnect

The bullish case improves if Coherent keeps converting its sold-out backlog into revenue on schedule and gross margin keeps climbing toward 42%. Optical networking suppliers are sliding again, and Applied Optoelectronics (NASDAQ:AAOI) stock is falling the most as doubts about how artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure gets funded spread through the group. Applied Optoelectronics stock is at $88.99, down 9% in afternoon trading, though it remains up 155% year to date.
Meanwhile, Coherent Corp. (NYSE:COHR | COHR Price Prediction) stock is at $269.33, down 7% as it follows its smaller peer lower. Likewise, Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) stock is at $920.42, down 7% in step with Coherent. Such a tight range of losses points to a sector-wide revaluation of AI connectivity suppliers.
Thematic funds are feeling the pressure as well, and the Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF (CBOE:LYTE) is down 8%. Lumentum and Coherent were the fund’s two largest holdings as of August 6, while Applied Optoelectronics carried a far smaller weight in the basket. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is down 1%, a softer decline that shows how tightly the selling is concentrated in optical names.
Broadcom and Intel Funding Warnings Rattle Optical Names
Optical networking shares began selling off on October 12. The slide came after Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) chief executive Hock Tan stated access to capital could become a bigger constraint on AI expansion than chip shortages. Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) chief executive Lip-Bu Tan also pointed to rising borrowing costs and uncertainty over returns on AI investments. Along with other optical names, Lumentum stock finished among the market’s biggest losers that day.
The selling has continued since, and no company-specific development explains this session’s move in Applied Optoelectronics stock. Applied Optoelectronics completed an at-the-market equity program, raising capital to fund the capacity expansion its optical component business needs. Its completion announcement came on October 5, days before the funding warnings from Broadcom and Intel.
Smallest Supplier Faces the Biggest Capacity Test
Lasers, transceivers and optical components from Applied Optoelectronics, Coherent and Lumentum move data between servers inside AI data centers. Their revenue tracks hyperscale spending. So the group is sensitive to any sign that budgets could tighten (we covered seven non-chipmaker suppliers riding the same AI expansion in a free report here). By far the smallest of the group, Applied Optoelectronics also sells into cable broadband networks, which gives it a revenue base Coherent and Lumentum don’t share.
Record results support the bull case. In Q2 2026, Applied Optoelectronics posted revenue of $191.92 million, up 86.4% year over year, as its datacenter segment more than doubled. The company also returned to adjusted profitability, earning $0.06 per share against a $0.015 estimate.
On the company’s August 6 call, chief executive Thompson Lin stated, “Demand to support next-generation AI infrastructure remains so robust that our near-term revenue is bounded almost entirely by production capacity and key component availability.” Management then guided Q3 2026 revenue to $255 million to $290 million. Lin also forecast that demand would outpace production capacity through mid-2027.
Hyperscale Orders Decide the Expansion Payoff
The open question for Applied Optoelectronics is whether hyperscale customers keep placing orders at the pace its expanded capacity assumes. Its top 10 customers accounted for 99% of Q2 2026 revenue, which leaves little buffer if one large buyer slows down its spending or delays deliveries. Applied Optoelectronics still posted a net loss under generally accepted accounting principles in that quarter, a reminder that its rapid expansion is costly.
Coherent and Lumentum struck a confident tone in August. On an August 12 call, Coherent chief executive Jim Anderson stated, “We continue to see no signs of attenuation in customer demand.” Lumentum chief executive Michael Hurlston added that “data center architects are turning to optical links as a primary means of connectivity,” and the company guided Q1 FY2027 revenue to $1.225 billion to $1.275 billion.
Those remarks came weeks before the funding warnings from Broadcom and Intel, so fresh order commentary from these suppliers could show whether this pullback reflects a real shift in demand. For now, investors may want to keep their exposure to optical names appropriately sized for further volatility.

Coherent Corp. (NYSE:COHR | COHR Price Prediction) stock jumped 10% to $315.71 as traders focused on the company’s PhotonLink platform and fresh Wall Street support for AI infrastructure suppliers. Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) stock rose 9% to $1,058.42, while Corning (NYSE:GLW) stock advanced 3% to $158.89.
The broader optics rally outpaced the market. The Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF (CBOE:LYTE) gained 4% to $25.40, while the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE ARCA:SPY) slipped 0.2% to $761.11.
Coherent introduced PhotonLink in September as an integrated-optics platform for next-generation AI data centers. The company also expanded its Pluggable Optical Line System portfolio, linking chip-to-chip, inside-the-rack, and high-capacity data-center connectivity products to the same AI infrastructure buildout.
PhotonLink highlights Coherent’s vertically integrated position across materials, lasers, optics, specialty fibers, and related manufacturing capabilities. Coherent said the platform includes more than 10 customer engagements for co-packaged optics and more than 10 customer engagements for near-packaged optics.
AI data centers require more bandwidth and more efficient connections as workloads become larger and more complex. Coherent could benefit if hyperscalers and equipment makers accelerate deployments of advanced optical components, though the company must turn early engagement into sustained orders and profitable production.
Bernstein initiated coverage of Coherent with an Outperform rating as part of broader coverage of U.S. networking and optical companies. The research firm also began coverage of Lumentum, Ciena Corporation (NYSE:CIEN), and Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET) with Outperform ratings. Bernstein initiated Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) and Corning with Market Perform ratings, providing a more balanced view of an industry that has rallied sharply on AI-related expectations.
Coherent stock’s 10% gain exceeded the 4% move in the LYTE ETF, suggesting that PhotonLink and Bernstein’s favorable initiation gave traders a company-specific reason to bid up the shares. Still, Coherent stock can remain sensitive to shifts in AI capital-spending expectations, customer order timing, and concerns about industry capacity.

The company guided for fiscal first-quarter revenue between $1.225 billion and $1.275 billion. Lumentum management said demand signals for 2027 remained “incredibly strong,” while the company also reported that optical-circuit-switch shipments doubled from the fiscal third quarter to the fiscal fourth quarter.
Lumentum could benefit from demand for high-speed networking, optical switching, transceivers, and other hardware needed to connect AI computing systems. Yet Lumentum faces execution risk as the company expands output, with management previously acknowledging that shipments of high-powered lasers were behind demand.
Corning stock rose 3%, a smaller gain than Coherent stock and Lumentum stock but still well ahead of the SPY ETF’s 0.2% decline. Corning supplies specialty glass, fiber, and optical communications products, giving Corning multiple ways to participate in higher data-center connectivity spending.
The LYTE ETF’s 4% advance suggests the market’s buying interest extended beyond a single company. Coherent stock, Lumentum stock, and Corning stock all moved higher as traders returned to a group that benefits from expectations for rising AI network traffic and increasingly demanding data-center architectures.
The Coherent stock rally could continue if AI-related orders, customer commentary, and capital-spending plans remain supportive. However, the same theme creates risk if large customers delay infrastructure spending, if competitors build excess capacity, or if elevated expectations leave less room for execution mistakes.
Coherent has a compelling product catalyst in PhotonLink and a new Outperform rating to support the bullish discussion. CRDO vs. COHR: Which AI Connectivity Stock Is the Better Buy?
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:14 AM CDT 7 min read
Both Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd CRDO and Coherent Corp COHR are beneficiaries of the AI data center buildout, but approach the opportunity from different angles.
Credo specializes in high-speed connectivity solutions, including integrated circuits (ICs), retimers, optical DSPs, Active Electrical Cables (AECs), SerDes chiplets and SerDes IP licensing.
Coherent is a manufacturer of lasers, transceivers, optoelectronic devices and modules, and engineered materials for verticals spanning industrial, instrumentation, communications and electronics markets.
For investors, the choice between CRDO and COHR is not straightforward. Let us break down the fundamentals, valuations, growth outlook and risks for each company to determine which stock stands out.
As AI clusters grow larger, connectivity is emerging as a critical constraint. Management highlighted that the challenge is no longer just bandwidth, but also reliability, power efficiency, signal integrity, telemetry and serviceability. Credo believes its system-level approach, which combines silicon, firmware, manufacturing tests and qualification, remains a key differentiator.
AEC is a system-level product for CRDO and its core growth engine. The company now has deep relationships with five hyperscalers, alongside expanding engagement with Neocloud customers. Credo continues to see higher AEC penetration within existing customers as deployments scale, while the shift toward 200-gig-per-lane 1.6T ports provides another growth opportunity.
The retimer business is another lucrative opportunity. Management noted that the retimer business also delivered record quarterly revenues, supported by scale-up deployments of Screaming Eagle at 100-gig-per-lane and initial contributions from its 200-gig-per-lane Blue Heron retimer.
The most significant shift in Credo's business mix is unfolding in its optical segment. On the last earnings call, management added that it continues to project more than $600 million in optical revenues, with ZeroFlap optics, silicon photonics PICs and optical DSPs each contributing over $100 million. Credo added that its optical DSP business generated "record revenues" in the fiscal first quarter. The company also recognized its first silicon-photonics PIC revenues following the DustPhotonics acquisition, with initial wins involving 800-gig and 1.6T optical transceivers. Credo continues to forecast more than 85% year-over-year revenue growth for fiscal 2027, aided by an expected second-half inflection.
The company's recent product announcements further strengthen its growth prospects. At the October 2026 OCP Global Summit, the company introduced its 1.6T ZeroFlap Active Light Cable ("ALC"). The wide-parallel optical interconnect solution is built for next-generation AI infrastructure, addressing rising reliability and energy-efficiency requirements. The solution targets AI scale-out and front-end networks, strengthening Credo's position in next-generation optical interconnects. Shipments are expected to begin in 2027.
Alongside the new ALC, the company announced the launch of the Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics Workstream within the Open Compute Project community. The initiative, backed by a leading hyperscaler and optical technology providers, including AFL, ams OSRAM and BizLink, aims to advance the development of the wide, parallel optical connectivity ecosystem.
The latest developments build on the company's expanding product portfolio. In September 2026, Credo launched its new family of 224G-based ZF optical transceivers. The new products extend Credo's ZF architecture to 1.6T port speeds and combine its 224G-per-lane optical DSP with the Kfir200 silicon photonics-based PICs and latest-generation PILOT diagnostics platform. The products are available in 2xDR4, 2xFR4 and DR8 configurations, supporting a range of AI scale-out interconnect architectures.
CRDO's growth does not come without meaningful risks. In the fiscal first quarter, four customers generated roughly 84% of quarterly revenues. Customer concentration is a major concern as it exposes the company to shifts in customer spending decisions and could materially affect results.
Execution risk is another risk factor. Much of the expected growth in fiscal 2027 is dependent on a successful ramp in the optical business. Any delay in deployment or broader industry transitions could affect this ramp. Macroeconomic uncertainties and exposure to the AI investment cycle amid increasing market competition remain additional concerns. The DustPhotonics acquisition also reduced its cash balance to $764.3 million at the end of the fiscal first quarter.
Explosive growth in AI data center infrastructure is driving unprecedented demand for optical networking solutions, positioning Coherent for long-term growth.
The Datacenter & Communications segment remains Coherent's core engine, contributing 79% of total revenues in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. Segment revenues increased 59% year over year, while data center revenues surged 66% on broad-based strength. Growing adoption of 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers bodes well. Management expects the 1.6T transceiver ramp to accelerate in calendar 2026 and 2027 as customer adoption increases.
Coherent expects first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues between $2.2 billion and $2.4 billion, with non-GAAP earnings per share of $1.85-$2.05. The company expects to achieve its first-ever quarter with over $3 billion in revenue by the end of fiscal 2027.
The launch of PhotonLink strengthens its product portfolio. This integrated optics platform combines lasers, silicon photonics, specialty fibers, isolators, specialty fibers, micro-optics and detectors to support co-packaged optics ("CPO"), near-packaged optics ("NPO") and emerging chip-to-chip connectivity. PhotonLink-related revenues are expected to begin ramping in the fourth quarter of calendar 2026.
Beyond transceivers, CPO, multi-rail systems, optical circuit switching ("OCS") and advanced materials for data center, thermal and power management offer additional growth opportunities. OCS revenues increased sequentially in the fiscal fourth quarter, while multi-rail revenues are expected to begin ramping in the first half of calendar 2027. The company expects OCS revenues to improve, supported by capacity expansion, in the upcoming quarters.
On the last earnings call, COHR noted that OCS represented more than $4 billion of addressable opportunity across data center interconnect, scale-up and scale-out networks. Further, management added that CPO, NPO and other forms of integrated optics represent more than $15 billion of incremental addressable opportunity over the coming years as these technologies enable the transition from copper connectivity.
Aggressive capacity expansion strategy bodes well. On the last earnings call, management said that the company was expanding its six-inch indium phosphide production capacity, targeting a doubling of internal output year over year by the end of the first quarter of fiscal 2027. Management expects capacity to more than double again by the end of calendar 2027.
However, the company is witnessing rising operating and capital expenses as it focuses on capacity expansion. While these investments are necessary for long-term growth, they may pressure margins and free cash flow if revenues do not materialize as expected. Capital expenditures reached $556 million in the fiscal fourth quarter, compared with $290 million in the preceding quarter, and management expects further sequential increase in the fiscal first quarter.
Heavy reliance on the Datacenter & Communications segment increases volatility linked to AI spending cycles amid increasing competition and macroeconomic troubles. Weakness in the Industrial segment, owing to softness in broader industrial markets, is concerning.
Price Performance & Valuations of CRDO & COHR
Year to date, CRDO and COHR are up 24.5% and 42.6%, respectively.
CRDO is trading at a forward price-to-earnings multiple of 23.41X, lower than COHR's 24.73X.

Analysts have raised their earnings estimates for COHR by 0.9% for the current fiscal year in the past 60 days.
Estimates have been revised up 4.2% for CRDO's bottom line in the same period.
CRDO offers strong revenue growth prospects but customer concentration and execution risks remain concerns. COHR benefits from a broader optical portfolio, expanding manufacturing capacity and strong AI-driven demand, though rising capital expenditures could pressure cash flow.
